title: Length search register run
statement: Let $C,e,B,F$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $f$ map finite bit strings to finite bit strings, let $h$ be a finite bit string, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of fourteen registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$, register $12$ has value at most $F$, and $F$ is at most the value in register $7$. Assume that for every $i$ smaller than the value in register $7$, the length oracle for $f$ on the encoded pair $(h,i)$ returns true exactly when $i<F$. Then the computation can run from its length-bound state with register vector $v$ and no answer to its double-test state with register $12$ set to $F$ and no answer, with every configuration before the endpoint satisfying the program’s instruction-side conditions and register bound $B$.
